clips.text_zh: 我六月見BTC $60k，全年人哋話十月會大劈，我冇買。依家十月，BTC仲喺$80k樓上。到底發生咗事？仲有冇機會跌返落$50k？今次係咪真係上唔到車？🙏 又係食龜
clips.text_en_b1: >be me >saw BTC at $60k in June >everyone kept saying the biggest crypto bloodbath would be in October >didn't buy >It's October now >BTC is above $80k. What the fuck happened? What are the odds Bitcoin falls under $50k again? Am I actually priced out for real this time?
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon missed BTC at 60k, watching it sit above 80k in October

signal.rationale: Anon's pain post (op) is regret for not buying BTC at 60k, but no real entry thesis given

clips.text_en_b2: >be me in June, staring at BTC stuck around $60k >literally everyone in /biz/ insisted we'd get hit with the mother of all crypto bloodbaths in October >shrugged it off and didn't touch it. Now look at me, BTC is hovering comfortably above $80k and I'm left scratching my head. What actually went down this autumn? Is there any genuine chance it tanks below $50k again, or am I genuinely priced out for good? Seems like the universe is dead set on handing me the…
clips.text_en_c1: Back in June, I watched Bitcoin hovering around the $60k mark, fully expecting the much-anticipated October bloodbath that every crypto commentator had been insisting was inevitable. I deliberately held off on buying, assuming the dip would materialise. Fast forward to October: BTC is comfortably trading north of $80k, and I am left wondering what on earth actually transpired. The question that genuinely haunts me is whether there remains any realistic probability of a correction back toward the $50k range, or whether I have, for once and for all, been permanently priced out of a generational rally while I waited for a crash that never came.
clips.text_en_c2: In June of this year Bitcoin sat near sixty thousand dollars, and the consensus across virtually every crypto forum was unequivocal: October would deliver a catastrophic correction, the kind of capitulation event that retail bagholders had been bracing for since the previous cycle's blow-off top. I, being the cautious sort, declined to enter any position, and lo and behold, the dreaded month has arrived and BTC is trading comfortably north of eighty grand with no bloodbath in sight. One is compelled to ask what, precisely, the perma-bears were pricing in. Are the odds of a sub-fifty-thousand retest now vanishingly small, or have I genuinely been priced out of this market for the remainder of the cycle? Once more, the tortoise prevails.

clips.text_zh: Sailor Moon吖，你有冇記住set個50/50 MSTR同SpaceX組合？btw Musk嘢永遠都係topic 🚀👍 我個prop firm帳戶又輸緊，睇住啲tech股流口水
clips.text_en_b1: Sailor Moon. You did remember to build a 50/50 MSTR and SpaceX portfolio, right, Anon? The thread is joking that anyone who split between MicroStrategy and SpaceX exposure would be quietly printing while the rest of /biz/ argues about memecoins.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ joke thread about a 50/50 MSTR and SpaceX portfolio

signal.rationale: Anon implies MSTR plus SpaceX-style exposure is the only winning portfolio right now

clips.text_en_b2: Honestly, Sailor Moon, you must have set up that 50/50 split between MSTR and SpaceX exposure, right Anon? Because the joke running through the thread is crystal clear: anyone who quietly allocated half their capital to MicroStrategy and the other half to SpaceX has been busy printing money in the background while the rest of /biz/ loses its mind over memecoins. Meanwhile Musk-related plays never stop being the talk of the board.
clips.text_en_c1: Sailor Moon, you did remember to construct that balanced 50/50 portfolio split between MicroStrategy and SpaceX exposure, didn't you? The thread's running gag is that anyone who allocated capital across those two vehicles would be quietly compounding serious gains in the background while the remainder of the board obsesses over the latest memecoin speculation. Meanwhile, my funded trading account is bleeding red for the third consecutive week, and I find myself staring at the tech sector with unconcealed envy. There is a particular kind of pain that comes from watching a thesis vindicated without having had the conviction to back it properly.
clips.text_en_c2: Sailor Moon's much-maligned fifty-fifty allocation between MicroStrategy and SpaceX, which /biz/ spent months deriding as a clownish exercise in unbridled techno-utopianism, has quietly outperformed the entire speculative memecoin complex by an almost indecent margin. While Anons bickered furiously over the latest dog-themed derivative or whichever AI vapourware token was pumping that particular hour, anyone who simply split capital between Saylor's leveraged Bitcoin proxy and Musk's orbital ambitions was, unbeknownst to them, compounding at a rate that would render even the most cynical lurker's portfolio a fait accompli. The thesis, as it turns out, was almost embarrassingly correct. My own prop firm account, meanwhile, continues its inexorable bleed, and I observe those very equities with the wistful resignation of a man watching the parade from the pavement.

clips.text_zh: Elon個X係全互聯網唯一冇大bot問題嘅平台，大部分用戶同post都係真人🤔 到底呢條友係神級CS head，定係其他網嘅bot都係佢放出嚟？wtf lol
clips.text_en_b1: Elon Musk's signature website, X, is the only website that doesn't have a major botting problem and still has mostly human users and posts. Is this guy either the greatest cybersecurity mind alive, or is he personally responsible for botting the rest of the internet?
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread arguing X has no bots while the rest of the web is full of them
clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk's signature platform, X, is apparently the only major website on the entire internet that doesn't have a substantial bot problem, and still mostly consists of actual human users posting genuine content. Which honestly raises a serious question: is this guy genuinely the greatest cybersecurity mind of our generation, or is he somehow personally responsible for unleashing bots across every other competing platform? Because one of those two explanations has to be true, and neither sounds particularly reassuring.
clips.text_en_c1: Elon Musk's flagship platform, X, is apparently the singular corner of the internet that has managed to evade the bot infestation plaguing virtually every other major social network, with engagement that remains, by and large, the product of real human activity. The proposition inevitably invites one of two interpretations: either Musk is the most formidable cybersecurity strategist of our generation, having cracked the code on authenticity verification, or, somewhat more troublingly, he bears personal responsibility for unleashing the very bot armies he now claims to have defeated elsewhere. Neither reading is comfortable, and that ambiguity is precisely the point.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk's flagship acquisition, X, has apparently become the singular outpost on the entire internet where bot infestation remains a marginal rather than existential phenomenon, its posts and interactions being, ostensibly, the genuine output of carbon-based users who occasionally eat, sleep, and argue about cryptocurrency. The epistemic implications of this curious anomaly are rather difficult to dismiss: either Musk is, in some unfathomable sense, the preeminent cybersecurity savant of our generation, a Prometheus bestowing digital hygiene upon a benighted web, or — and the circumstantial evidence here becomes rather more compelling — he is, in fact, the principal architect of every botnet plaguing competing platforms, a puppeteer whose marionettes swarm the digital commons while his own garden remains conspicuously, almost suspiciously, verdant. The logical conclusion is, charitably, left to the reader.

clips.text_zh: 原來2019年英國劇Years & Years已經畫晒個globalist劇本：大疫情、lockdown、美中南海開戰、Abraham Accords搞掂巴勒斯坦…😭 真係睇到標冷汗 ok我返去做GI report
clips.text_en_b1: The Globalist Plan is apparently already outlined in the British TV show Years & Years from 2019. The show predicted a big pandemic with lockdowns, the US attacking China in the South China Sea, the Palestine question being neutralized via the Abraham Accords, and Russia taking Ukraine.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread claiming a 2019 BBC show predicted current geopolitics
clips.text_en_b2: Turns out the so-called Globalist Plan was already laid out in painstaking detail by the 2019 British series Years & Years, which somehow managed to predict a devastating global pandemic complete with sweeping lockdowns, a full-scale US military strike in the South China Sea targeting China, the Palestine conflict being conveniently neutralised through the Abraham Accords, and Russia ultimately moving on Ukraine. Watching that show back now genuinely gives me cold sweats, because the accuracy is almost unsettling.
clips.text_en_c1: It turns out that the so-called globalist playbook was already laid out, with eerie precision, in the 2019 British dystopian series Years & Years, which anticipated a devastating pandemic accompanied by sweeping restrictions, escalating great-power tensions culminating in a US-China confrontation across the South China Sea, a neatly resolved Palestinian question courtesy of the Abraham Accords framework, and an inexorable Russian advance into Ukrainian territory. Watching the episodes in retrospect, one cannot help but break out in a cold sweat at how closely speculative fiction has tracked unfolding geopolitical reality, and I find myself quietly retreating back to my gastrointestinal report, where at least the conclusions remain mercifully fictional.
clips.text_en_c2: The Russell T Davies script, which aired a mere six years ago, appears to have functioned less as speculative drama than as a rather meticulous architectural blueprint for the subsequent decade of geopolitical theatre, anticipating with unnerving fidelity the pandemic, the ensuing lockdowns, the prospective Sino-American confrontation in the South China Sea, and the Abraham Accords' curious resolution of the Palestinian question. One watches with a mounting sense of vertigo, recognising each unfolding crisis as though it had been pre-screened in a Channel 4 writer's room. Whether one attributes this to prescience, self-fulfilling narrative, or merely the well-documented tendency of policymakers to plagiarise speculative fiction wholesale, the effect is, at minimum, profoundly disquieting. Right, I'm off to finish my gastrointestinal report; the patient, at least, is mercifully fictional.

clips.text_zh: 我而家日日deadlift 4pl8+，但越嚟越覺得自己唔健康、唔瘦、冇時間。gym純粹係喺度chasing PR🙏 真係要退後一步，肥仔信成日笑我點解唔做返cardio
clips.text_en_b1: How do I get out of the numbers big lifts swamp mentality? It's a never-ending black hole of chasing numbers at the detriment of everything else. I'm not healthier, I'm not leaner, I don't save up time. Outside of an actual competition anything over let's say 4pl8 deadlift 1RM is pointless.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about being stuck chasing deadlift PRs
clips.text_en_b2: How on earth do I drag myself out of this obsessive numbers-swamp mentality around heavy compound lifts? It's become this endless black hole where I'm constantly chasing bigger PRs at the expense of literally everything else that matters. I'm not healthier, I'm certainly not leaner, and I'm definitely not saving any time in the process. Outside of an actual sanctioned competition, anything beyond a 4pl8 deadlift 1RM is frankly pointless, even though my chubby friends keep ribbing me about doing some cardio for once.
clips.text_en_c1: How does one extricate oneself from the numbers-swamp mentality that progressively colonises every other consideration in training? I am now deadlifting comfortably above four plates, yet I find myself no healthier, no leaner, and demonstrably no better off in terms of time or general wellbeing than when I started. The entire enterprise feels like an inexorable black hole, in which chasing ever-more-impressive personal records has gradually come at the expense of everything that ostensibly justified the pursuit in the first place. Unless one is preparing for an actual sanctioned competition, anything beyond a four-plate deadlift one-rep max is, by any rational measure, pure diminishing returns.
clips.text_en_c2: The iron game, as any seasoned lifter will attest, possesses a peculiar gravitational pull toward what might best be described as numerical nihilism, a Sisyphean compulsion whereby one pursues ever more grotesque single-rep maxima at the expense of every other conceivable metric of well-being. I presently deadlift comfortably north of four plates and yet, paradoxically, find myself no leaner, no healthier, and demonstrably no less time-poor than when I began; the pursuit of incremental PRs has, in essence, devoured the very life it was ostensibly meant to enhance. Outside the narrow confines of sanctioned competition, anything beyond a respectable threshold is, I must concede, performative rather than purposeful. The ectomorphic brethren, whom I once disdained, may yet have the last laugh; perhaps cardio, that much-maligned discipline, deserves a rehabilitated place in the programme.

clips.text_zh: Ghost in the Shell套新動畫播完即冇人記得，1995年果套先係神🧐 The Matrix都係睇呢套啟發嘅。原版漫畫基本上無乜人睇過lol
clips.text_en_b1: >"Finally Ghost in The Shell is getting a REAL adaptation of the REAL story, unlike the dumb melodramatic movie!" >Anime comes and goes making zero impact whatsoever, and is forgotten immediately after airing. There's a reason 90% of people loved the 1995 movie. It inspired The Matrix. The original manga has inspired practically no one.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread roasting the new Ghost in the Shell anime
clips.text_en_b2: >"Finally Ghost in the Shell is getting a proper, faithful adaptation of the actual source material — unlike that overrated, dumb melodramatic 1995 movie!" >The anime promptly airs, makes absolutely zero cultural impact whatsoever, and gets completely forgotten the moment the final episode drops. There's a very good reason roughly 90% of people fell head over back for the 1995 film: it directly inspired The Matrix and reshaped sci-fi cinema forever. Meanwhile, the original manga, which technically started it all, has inspired practically nobody.
clips.text_en_c1: The internet, for once, was almost unanimous in its pronouncement: finally, a Ghost in the Shell adaptation that would honour the source material rather than the comparatively sentimental 1995 film, whose romantic subplot had long frustrated purists who insisted that Shirow Masamune's original manga was the definitive text. The new anime promptly aired, generated precisely zero cultural footprint, and was forgotten almost immediately. There is a fairly obvious reason why roughly ninety percent of audiences still revere the Mamoru Oshii film: it was conceptually radical enough to inspire The Matrix itself, whereas the original manga, despite its obvious influence, has inspired practically no subsequent creators.
clips.text_en_c2: The collective enthusiasm which greeted the announcement of a 'faithful' Ghost in the Shell adaptation, one that would supposedly restore Masamune Shirow's densely philosophical source material to its rightful prominence after the perceived melodramatic liberties of Oshii's nineties classic, has, in rather predictable fashion, dissipated with unseemly haste. The anime arrived, registered barely a blip upon the cultural seismograph, and vanished into the churning void of seasonal releases, leaving scarcely a critical footprint. The 1995 film endures, of course, for reasons that subsequent iterations have conspicuously failed to replicate; its philosophical density and visual grammar quite literally gave birth to The Wachowskis' Matrix, an influence so foundational it scarcely requires elaboration. Shirow's original manga, by contrast, remains a magnificently abstruse artefact, admired by a coterie of devotees and, alas, inspiring virtually no one beyond them.

clips.text_zh: 13年開發、15億美金budget，就換嚟少少畫面提升🤡 工程師睇到都想喊。睇返我自己FE準備嗰幾本soil nailing同load path書，起碼有factor of safetylol
clips.text_en_b1: Rockstar sissies... 13 years of development and 1.5 billion dollars, and the actual visual improvement on screen is this small? Anons are comparing the trailer side by side with GTA V and the leap is way smaller than Rockstar's budget would suggest.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread mocking Rockstar's 1.5B GTA 6 budget vs visible improvement

signal.rationale: Gaming industry commentary, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Honestly, Rockstar have completely lost the plot this time around. Thirteen long years of development and an eye-watering 1.5 billion dollar budget, and the actual on-screen visual improvement is genuinely this underwhelming? People are doing side-by-side comparisons of the new trailer against GTA V, and the leap forward is absurdly small given how much money and time was supposedly thrown at the project.
clips.text_en_c1: Rockstar's development cycle has stretched across what is, by any reasonable industry metric, an almost unprecedented thirteen years, accompanied by a production budget that, at roughly one and a half billion dollars, dwarfs virtually every comparable title in the medium's history. The visual delta over the preceding GTA V, however, appears strikingly modest when frames are placed side by side, prompting widespread incredulity among anons who had expected generational leaps commensurate with the expenditure. As a practising structural engineer, I cannot help but note that my own preparation for the FE exam, involving soil nailing design manuals and load path analyses, offered rather more tangible returns than Rockstar's decade-long, nine-figure…
clips.text_en_c2: Rockstar's prodigal return after a thirteen-year development cycle, a gestation period during which an eye-watering one-point-five billion dollars was lavished upon what was, by all reasonable expectation, meant to be a generational leap in interactive visual fidelity, has produced, upon close inspection of the inaugural trailer, something rather more underwhelming than the budget would lead a reasonable observer to anticipate. The frame-by-frame comparisons with its 2013 predecessor, conducted with forensic enthusiasm by Anons across /v/, reveal improvements that, while technically present, fall considerably short of the quantum leap that half a decade of crunch and nine-figure expenditure ought, in any just universe, to have delivered. One wonders whether the engineers who toiled through those years feel the same vertiginous sense of disproportion.

clips.text_zh: 有個/biz/仔想完全離開金融system，自己買地、種嘢食、雨水collect…🙏 但我連prop firm帳戶都輸緊，唔好話farm，繼續做underground utility survey先算lol
clips.text_en_b1: How do I detach myself from the financial system? Knowing I can't get rid of property taxes, is there a way to avoid them anywhere in the world? I have savings so it should not be a problem to buy land and the tools to be self-sufficient — anvil, oven, oil press, rain water collection, the whole off-grid setup.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about going fully off-grid to escape property taxes

signal.rationale: Lifestyle escape fantasy, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: There's a guy over on /biz/ actively trying to detach himself entirely from the whole financial system, because he's got enough savings to actually buy land and kit himself out with the full off-grid setup — an anvil, a proper oven, an oil press, rain water collection, the lot. His sticking point, though, is that property taxes seem basically inescapable no matter which country he relocates to.
clips.text_en_c1: There is a recurring strain of /biz/ poster who fantasises about entirely detaching from the financial system, purchasing acreage outright, and pursuing a fully self-sufficient existence: an off-grid homestead complete with a forge, a wood-fired oven, an oil press for home rendering, and rainwater harvesting sufficient to render municipal utilities irrelevant. The aspiration presupposes, of course, that one can somehow circumvent the universally inescapable burden of property taxation, which the poster optimistically assumes their accumulated savings will comfortably absorb.
clips.text_en_c2: The proposition of absenting oneself entirely from the labyrinthine apparatus of contemporary monetary exchange, of acquiring a parcel of land somewhere sufficiently remote that the long arm of property taxation cannot reach, and thereafter cultivating one's own sustenance via forge, oven, oil press, and a meticulously engineered rainwater harvesting system, is, on the surface, an exercise in admirable radicalism. /biz/'s homesteading fantasist had savings sufficient to underwrite the experiment; the theoretical apparatus was, at least, coherent. My own circumstances, by contrast, render such fantasies risible: my prop firm account continues its stately haemorrhage of capital, my ambitions of agrarian self-sufficiency remain firmly consigned to the realm of speculative fiction, and my present occupation consists of conducting underground utility surveys beneath the boots of contractors who, unlike me, apparently possess functional risk management protocols.
